verifications.claim: For those born in 1960 or later, full retirement age is 67.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "FRA is age 67 ... born in 1960 or later"; "1960 and later 67"; "born in 1960 or later . . . age 67"; table "1960 and later 67"; table "1960 and later 67"
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources, including official SSA pages, directly state FRA is 67 for those born 1960 or later.

verifications.claim: Full Retirement Age for Social Security for those born 1954 or earlier is 65–66.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.reasoning: Sources support FRA of 66 for 1943-1954 (including 1954) and 65 or gradual increase prior, but no direct statement of '65-66' range for '1954 or earlier'; approximation via tables.

verifications.claim: Full Retirement Age for Social Security for those born 1955–1959 is 66 and 2–10 months.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "born in 1959, ... 66 and 10 months"; "1955 66 and 2 months ... 1959 66 and 10 months"; "born between 1955 and 1959 . . . increases by two months"; table "1955 66 and 2 months ... 1959 66 and 10 months"; table same
verifications.reasoning: Directly matches detailed birth year breakdowns in multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Full Retirement Age for Social Security for those born 1960 or later is 67.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "FRA ... 67 for those born in 1960 or later"; "1960 and later 67"; "born in 1960 or later ... 67"; table "1960 and later 67"; table "1960 and later 67"
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly stated across official and cited sources.

verifications.claim: Social Security benefits can start at 62 but are permanently reduced.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "start receiving retirement benefits before your full retirement age, your benefits are reduced"; "earliest ... age 62"; "Earliest age ... 62 ... claiming before ... reduced monthly benefits"; "start ... as early as age 62 ... benefits will be reduced ... before your full retirement age"
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm earliest age 62 with permanent reduction for early claiming.

verifications.claim: Delayed retirement increases benefits by ~8% annually up to age 70.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "adding up to 8% for each full year ... until age 70"; "increase your monthly benefit by about eight percent for each year ... up to age 70"; "8% more ... until age 70"
verifications.reasoning: Precise match on ~8% per year delayed credits up to 70.

verifications.claim: Social Security replaces approximately 40% of the average wage earner's income.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "Social Security retirement benefits replace 40 percent of pre-retirement income"; same in R7
verifications.reasoning: Direct quote from DOL sources on average replacement rate.

verifications.claim: It is possible to work and receive benefits while retired.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "continue working while collecting Social Security"; "You can continue working and start receiving your retirement benefits ... You can get Social Security retirement benefits and work at the same time"
verifications.reasoning: Explicitly allowed in SSA sources, with earnings test details.

verifications.claim: Social Security benefits may be temporarily reduced if under full retirement age and earn over a certain limit.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "temporarily withholds $1 ... earned above $24,480"; "benefits will be reduced if you earn more than the yearly earnings limits ... recalculate ... credit"; "benefits could be reduced if your earnings exceed a certain limit ... recomputed to give you credit"
verifications.reasoning: Sources describe earnings test as temporary reduction/withholding before FRA, with later recalculation.
